title: Why Eurasia, Not the Indo-Pacific, Matters Most in Next Phase of Taiwan Deterrence
gist: The authors argue China is building overland energy and trade resilience (Central Asian pipelines, Power of Siberia 2, rationing capacity shown in the Q2 2026 Hormuz shock) to blunt a Malacca blockade, which could embolden it over Taiwan. U.S. deterrence should therefore target Eurasian corridor swing states (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan and the Ganja Gap), for example by redirecting part of Japan's $550 billion trade-deal investment pledge to third-country infrastructure.

insights.claim: Roughly 75-80 percent of China's seaborne oil imports pass through the Strait of Malacca, and Chinese strategists have long tied this vulnerability to Beijing's freedom of action over Taiwan.

themes.theme: Hormuz shock as blockade dry run

insights.claim: Per the U.S. EIA, China imported just 8.1 million b/d of crude in Q2 2026, 32 percent less than the prior quarter, while strategic inventories fell only 49 million barrels (1.54 to 1.49 billion), which means Beijing absorbed the Hormuz shock mainly by cutting refinery runs rather than draining reserves.
insights.speaker: Ken Moriyasu and William Pazos
insights.so_what: China's demand elasticity in crises is higher than assumed; in supply shocks, Chinese refinery-run cuts can cap crude price spikes while hurting product exports.

insights.claim: Kazakhstan (flat terrain, extensive rail to the Caspian), Uzbekistan (future hub of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, linking to Turkmenistan and Iran) and Azerbaijan are the three most important states for China's overland connectivity.

insights.claim: The Ganja Gap, a corridor about 60 km wide linking Azerbaijan and Georgia, carries oil and gas pipelines and the Baku-Tbilisi-Kars railway and is the hinge of the trans-Caspian Middle Corridor for Asia-Europe trade that avoids Russia and Iran, making it effectively 'Malacca on land'.
insights.speaker: Ken Moriyasu and William Pazos
insights.so_what: A single-point chokepoint for Middle Corridor trade and Caspian energy; geopolitical risk there affects Caspian oil/gas flows and Eurasian logistics.
insights.quote: It is, in effect, Malacca on land.
